title: EventEmitter and custom pub/sub APIs
hook: Node's EventEmitter is the reference pub/sub implementation: named events, multiple listeners, error propagation, and memory-leak warnings when you forget to remove handlers.

blocks.text: **EventEmitter** maintains a map of event names to listener arrays. **emit(event, ...args)** synchronously invokes all listeners registered with **on/once**. **once** auto-removes after first fire. Emitting `'error'` without a listener throws — special case. **off/removeListener** prevents leaks. Browser **EventTarget** (addEventListener) is the DOM parallel with capture/bubble; EventEmitter is flatter and Node-centric.

entries.plainDefinition: Publishers emit events; subscribers listen without direct references.
Callback registered for an event name — may be multiple per event.
Node warning when >10 listeners on one event — often a leak signal.
Web platform API — addEventListener/removeEventListener with event objects.

blocks.text: Streams, HTTP servers, WebSockets, and process signals in Node extend EventEmitter. Custom domain events decouple modules — payment emits `'captured'`, analytics listens. Leaked listeners retain closures and DOM — top interview and production issue. C# **event** keyword is typed and mostly single-cast; JS allows any string and multiple anonymous handlers.

blocks.title: Interview trap: emit is sync
blocks.body: Listeners run synchronously in registration order during emit — long listener blocks others. Defer heavy work with setImmediate or queue to worker.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: emit(event, payload)
items.body: Copy listener array, invoke each with payload.

items.title: once
items.body: Wrap fn to self-remove after first call.

items.title: off / removeAllListeners
items.body: Cleanup on shutdown or component unmount.

snippet.label: Minimal custom EventEmitter
snippet.explanation: Copy array before iterate so off inside listener does not skip siblings. on returns unsubscribe — React useEffect cleanup pattern.

snippet.label: Node EventEmitter with error handling
snippet.explanation: Always attach error listener on long-lived emitters — otherwise Node throws on unhandled error event.

snippet.label: C# event keyword
snippet.explanation: C# events are typed, multicast delegates, only invokable from declaring class. JS emit is public on the emitter instance.

snippet.label: Failure mode: listener leak
snippet.explanation: Return unsubscribe from on or call off in cleanup — same as removeEventListener in DOM.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: No error listener on EventEmitter. Anonymous on() without off — cannot remove later. Heavy work inside emit blocking all listeners. Assuming async listeners are awaited — emit does not wait.

blocks.text: Implement **typed emitter** wrappers in TS (mitt, typed-emitter) for compile-time event names. For microservices, prefer message queues over in-process EventEmitter at scale — emitter is single-process. Use **AbortSignal** to cascade cancellation through listener trees in modern code.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Not knowing error event throws without listener. Cannot implement minimal emitter or explain sync emit ordering. Confusing EventEmitter with Promise or async queue.

interviewTakeaways: EventEmitter: on/emit/off — listeners run synchronously in order.
Unhandled 'error' event throws in Node — always attach error listener.
Return unsubscribe function to prevent listener leaks.
60s: Pub/sub with string events. emit sync invokes all listeners. C# typed events, DOM EventTarget parallel. Leaks cause MaxListeners warning — off on cleanup.
Follow-up: implement once() and explain why copy listener array before loop.
commonPitfalls: Registering listeners in mount without cleanup on unmount.
Emitting error without handler crashing the process.
Strong answer: sync dispatch, error event special case, typed wrapper, compare C# multicast event.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Generic EventEmitter<{ paid: [order: Order] }> gives compile-time event names — bridges JS stringly events toward C# typed delegates.
Readable streams emit data, end, error — same listener model as custom domain buses.
